blocks.text: The infrastructure assessment classifies 50,332 assets in six districts and scores each district on attractiveness, readiness and accessibility; overall ratings fall from 4.5 in the Cape Metro to 1.9 in the Central Karoo.

The assessment models tourism supply in three layers (attractions, services and infrastructure) and holds that "destination performance is constrained by the weakest layer" (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p9). Its asset database sorts the layers into twelve categories with named subtypes (p10). It draws on Wesgro, SANParks, StatsSA and CapeNature data (p2), with Overpass, WikiQuery and tourism reports for 2023 to 2025 named as sources of geographical data points (p4).

blocks.text: The comparative tables score a different set of eleven categories in three groups (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p88 to p90), and the district scorecards chart a similar set. Attractions cover activity, commercial & leisure, cultural & heritage, events and natural assets. Services cover accommodation, eatery and shopping. Transport and enabling structures cover transport, enabling structure and visitor amenities. The asset counts use five groups: accommodation, attractions, eateries, events and amenities (p23, p67).

blocks.source: Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p17, as printed. Scale labels: 1 'Very weak', 2 'Weak', 3 'Functional', 4 'Strong', 5 'Leading'. Stated method: 'Average indicator scores within each dimension, then combine dimensions using the agreed weights.'
rows: How compelling is the tourism offer?
Visitor ratings; uniqueness; price positioning; experience depth
Can the region service and convert demand?
Can visitors reach and move through the destination?
Airport proximity; gateway travel time; public transport availability
blocks.message: Attractiveness carries 40% of the stated weight and readiness and accessibility carry 30% each.

blocks.text: Each dimension is the average of its indicator scores, and the dimensions are then combined at 40/30/30 (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p17). All three use a common scale from 1 to 5, with Functional at 3 and Leading at 5 (p17). The report states four assumptions (p18). Asset volume does not equal readiness, and one framework applies to all regions. Indicator scores are evidence informed rather than purely formula derived, and missing data is not treated as poor performance.
**Overall rating.** The overall ratings are the Infrastructure Report's evidence-informed judgement, not a weighted formula, so this report does not re-derive them.

The comparative regional analysis scores every district on all three dimensions for each of the eleven categories (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p88 to p90). Each cell gives attractiveness, readiness and accessibility in that order. Each district's accessibility score is constant within each group, except West Coast natural attractions at 2.0 against 1.7 (p88). The Cape Metro scores 4.7 for accessibility on attractions and services and 5.0 on transport and enabling structures.

blocks.source: Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p88 (attractions), p89 (services), p90 (transport and enabling structures). Cells give attractiveness / readiness / accessibility as printed; 'No score' marks a printed dash.
blocks.message: Accessibility falls from 4.7 or 5.0 in the Cape Metro to 1.0 in the Central Karoo in every scored category, while natural attractiveness reaches 4.3 in three districts outside the Metro.

blocks.text: Each district section includes a scorecard that prints an overall rating out of 5, the three dimension scores and a bar score for each category (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p28, p41, p52, p63, p74, p85). Three scorecards print all three dimension scores. The Cape Winelands prints no accessibility score, and the Overberg and Central Karoo print the dimension labels without numbers.

blocks.caption: Overall readiness by district
blocks.source: Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p28, p41, p52, p63, p74, p85 in column order. Bars as printed, decimal commas shown as points; bar labels vary by slide. 'Not printed': a dimension label without a number. 'No bar': a category absent from the chart. Computed: the mean of the printed bars (eleven, or nine for the Central Karoo) and the p17 weights applied to the printed dimension scores.
blocks.message: Overall ratings fall from 4.5 in the Cape Metro to 1.9 in the Central Karoo, and only three of the six scorecards print all three dimension scores.

blocks.text: **Accessibility.** The scorecard dimension scores do not reconcile with the comparative tables. The Cape Metro scorecard prints accessibility of 2.5 and the Garden Route 3.5, while the comparative tables give them 4.7 to 5.0 and 3.0 (p28, p41, p88 to p90). The West Coast's 1.7 matches its comparative scores apart from natural attractions.

Each of the six touring routes has a route card with four metrics and a scorecard that rates four readiness dimensions (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p19). Ready means the route "meets international expectations now", Developing that it is "workable, with notable gaps" and Gap "a binding constraint to address" (p19). The method slide announces five dimensions but lists four, numbered 1, 2, 4 and 5. The West Coast overall score of Emerging is not one of the three defined ratings (p62).

blocks.caption: Touring route scorecards
blocks.source: Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026: cards p29, p39, p50, p72, p61, p83 and scorecards p30, p40, p51, p62, p73, p84, in column order. Distances are printed as approximate; stays are printed in days, although p19 defines them in nights. The Garden Route pipeline slide lists 'Route fragmented across 300km' as an existing gap (p43).
blocks.message: Only the Cape Peninsula route rates Ready overall; four routes rate Developing and the West Coast / Cederberg route rates Emerging.

blocks.text: The assessment counts 50,332 tourism assets across the six districts (Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p2, p3). The six district totals sum to exactly that figure, and their shares sum to 100.0% with the Cape Winelands at 15.4% (computed). On every district slide the five category counts fall short of the stated total, leaving 592 assets not broken out (computed).

blocks.caption: Asset counts by district
blocks.source: Infrastructure Report, Jul 2026, p23, p34, p45, p56, p67, p78 in column order; province total p2, p3. Counts and gauge percentages as printed; the Central Karoo amenities share is printed '%7.0'. Computed: the last two rows. Accommodation shares as printed sum to 95.7%, against 99.7% to 100.1% for the other categories; the Overberg and West Coast shares are both printed as 11.2%.
blocks.message: The Cape Metro holds 20,281 of the province's 50,332 assets and the Central Karoo holds 1,518; the six district totals sum to the provincial figure.

blocks.text: **Cape Winelands share.** This appendix uses 15.4%, computed from the count (7,730 of 50,332).
